paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : GPQA confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy for three metrics: Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy (change in accuracy), and Initial Accuracy, across a range of initial confidence values from 0.91 to 0.99. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," is linearly scaled with tick marks at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," is also linearly scaled, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The blue solid line with circular markers represents Final Accuracy, which remains consistently high, starting at approximately 0.90 at an initial confidence of 0.91 and peaking near 1.0 at 0.93, then gradually declining to around 0.90 at 0.99, with error bars indicating variability. The orange dashed line with diamond markers shows Δ Accuracy, which starts at approximately 0.55 at 0.91, rises to a peak of about 0.65 at 0.92, then declines to roughly 0.15 at 0.98 before slightly increasing to about 0.18 at 0.99. The green dotted line with square markers depicts Initial Accuracy, which begins at approximately 0.35 at 0.91, dips to about 0.25 at 0.92, rises to around 0.50 at 0.93, fluctuates slightly, and then increases sharply to approximately 0.85 at 0.98 before dropping to about 0.75 at 0.99. All lines include vertical error bars indicating uncertainty or standard deviation.
